note: Un piatto proposto per ogni paese. È una proposta di lavoro, non un'affermazione: nessun piatto è dichiarato 'nazionale' finché una fonte seria non lo dice. La scelta va confermata caso per caso prima di ricercare la scheda; dove la fiducia è bassa, il nome stesso va verificato.
criteria: Un piatto noto e documentato in almeno una fonte non enciclopedica.
Un piatto diverso per ogni paese: dove due paesi condividono un piatto (moambe, couscous, ugali, nsima) si sceglie un'alternativa o si fa una scheda unica.
Dove una storia esiste già (injera, jollof, manioca) la scheda la richiama e non la ripete.
Nessuna scheda dice che un piatto è 'nazionale' senza una fonte che lo dica: i giornali lo ripetono spesso e sbagliano.

DZA.note: couscous is the better known; kept for the shared couscous story

BEN.note: pâte rouge; another option is wagashi (cheese)

BFA.note: with a leaf or okra sauce

BDI.note: Red kidney beans stewed with onion and chilli; sources agree beans are the everyday staple (about once a day per person, according to a travel guide). Confirmed as a dish; not to be called 'the' national dish.

CAF.note: Cassava porridge (gozo) with a long-simmered stew of cassava leaves, smoked fish or meat and palm oil (kanda). Confirmed as an everyday plate in several food sources.

COM.note: another option is langouste à la vanille

COG.note: shared with Gabon and DR Congo: choose a different dish if the three cards would repeat

CIV.note: with fish; on UNESCO's intangible heritage list (to verify in a source)

COD.note: cassava leaves; moambe is shared with Congo

GNQ.note: Replaces 'succotash', which no source supported. Spicy fish soup named as the signature dish by several food sources; confirm in the card.

ERI.note: spiced stew eaten with injera; shared with Ethiopia

SWZ.note: maize porridge with meat or vegetables

ETH.note: injera already has its own story

GMB.note: a draft card already exists (domoda); do not call it the national dish without a good source

GIN.note: Rice with a sauce of cooked leaves (sweet potato, cassava, okra) and smoked fish or meat. Confirmed as a family of dishes; fouti is an alternative.

MWI.note: with relish; Zambia's card must differ (ifisashi)

MRT.note: Confirmed as a festive dish; note that thieboudienne is also called Mauritania's national dish by some sources, but it is shared with Senegal, so the méchoui is kept for Mauritania.

MAR.note: couscous is shared with Algeria and Tunisia

MOZ.note: cassava leaves and peanuts or coconut

SEN.note: the jollof story already covers its origin; a card can focus on the dish itself

SSD.note: A thin fermented sorghum pancake, eaten in Sudan and South Sudan; one source calls it South Sudan's national dish, to verify. Sudan's card is ful medames.

SDN.note: shared with Egypt; kisra or gurasa are alternatives

TZA.note: Replaces ugali, shared with Kenya. Pilau with cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and cumin is described in several travel sources; ugali is called the national meal by others, so the choice is a judgement to revisit.
